hop3_docs: Dispositive motion | In law, a dispositive motion is a motion seeking a trial court order entirely disposing of all or part of the claims in favor of the moving party without need for further trial court proceedings.  "To dispose" of a claim means to "decide" the claim in favor of one or another party.  As a lawsuit may comprise numerous claims made by and against numerous parties, not every dispositive motion seeks to dispose of the entire lawsuit.  In the U.S., the most common type of dispositive motions seeking to dispose of the entire lawsuit are those for summary judgment.
